pp:me:2001:q7.title: GATE ME 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 7
pp:me:2001:q7.question: In the figure shown, the spring deflects by $\delta$ to position A ( the equilibrium position) when a mass m is kept on it. During free vibration, the mass is at position B at some instant. The change in potential energy of the spring-mass system from position A to position B is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \Delta(P E) &=(P E)_{B}-(P E)_{A} \\ &=\frac{1}{2} k(x+\delta)^{2}+0-\left[\frac{1}{2} k \delta^{2}+m g x\right] \end{aligned}$$

Taking reference datum at position B.

At equilibrium position i.e., at A.

$$\begin{array}{c} m g=\mathrm{k} \delta \\ \Delta(P E)=\frac{1}{2} k x^{2}+\frac{1}{2} k \delta^{2}+x k \delta-\frac{1}{2} k \delta^{2}-m g x\\ \text{as }\quad m g=k \delta\\ \Delta(P E)=\frac{1}{2} k x^{2}+\frac{1}{2} k \delta^{2}+m g x-\frac{1}{2} k \delta^{2}-m g x\\ =\frac{1}{2} k x^{2} \end{array}$$

Considering moment equilibrium condition about axis of rotation.

$$\begin{array}{l} 2 m l^{2} \ddot{\theta}+m g l \sin (\alpha+\theta)-m g l \sin (\alpha-\theta)=0 \\ \Rightarrow 2 m l^{2} \ddot{\theta}+m l g[\sin \alpha \cos \theta+\cos \alpha \sin \theta \\ \quad-\sin \alpha \cos \theta+\cos \alpha \cos \theta] \\ \Rightarrow 2 m l^{2} \ddot{\theta}+2 m g l \cos \alpha \sin \theta=0 \end{array}$$

For very small, $\theta, \sin \theta \approx \theta$

Hence, we get

$$\begin{array}{c} 2 m l^{2} \ddot{\theta}+2 m g l \cos \alpha=0 \\ \omega=\sqrt{\frac{2 m g l \cos \alpha}{2 m l^{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{g \cos \alpha}{l}} \end{array}$$

pp:me:2001:q40.title: GATE ME 2001 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:me:2001:q40.question: A small steam whistle (perfectly insulated and doing no shaft work) causes a drop of 0.8 kJ/kg in the enthalpy of steam from entry to exit. If the kinetic energy of the steam at entry is negligible, the velocity of the steam at exit is

primary.subtopicLabel: First Law, Heat, Work and Energy

detailed_solution.concept: Thermodynamics - First Law, Heat, Work and Energy
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given data:

$$\begin{aligned} \Delta h &=-0.8 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{2}-h_{1} &=-0.8 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{1}-h_{2} &=0.8 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}$$

Applying steady flow energy equation,

$h_{1}+\frac{V_{1}^{2}}{2}+g z_{1}+q=h_{2}+\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2}+g z_{2}+w$

Assumptions:

(i) q=0 adiabatic flow

(ii) w=0

(iii) Change k.E. and P.E. are neglect

(iv) Neglect inlet velocity.

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad h_{1} &=h_{2}+\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2} \\ h_{1} &=h_{2}+\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2000} \\ h_{1}-h_{2} &=\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2000} \\ \text{or}\qquad 8 &=\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2000} \\ V_{2}^{2} &=1600 \\ \text{or}\qquad V_{2} &=40 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$
